images.title: 16 rue Etienne-Marcel
images.author: VVVCFFrance
images.shows: whole facade: mascaron heads under balcony console brackets, richly molded window surrounds with alternating pediments, wrought-iron balconies -- textbook Third Republic ornament density

images.title: 53 rue Blanche
images.author: Pline
images.shows: whole facade, frontal: carved sculpted keystones/roundels above two window bands and an arched porte-cochere with carved surround -- 45-degree-comble roofline visible above

images.title: Angle rue Christiani, rue de Clignancourt
images.author: Jeanne Menjoulet
images.street: Angle rue Christiani / rue de Clignancourt, Paris 18e
images.shows: corner building with domed corner turret, columned window surrounds and continuous wrought-iron balconies -- shot from below at a raking upward angle and partly screened by street trees at ground level

images.title: Immeuble haussmannien (corner facade detail)
images.author: Dale Cruse
images.shows: close, mildly oblique crop of a corner facade: repeated carved lintel roundels above windows, dense wrought-iron balcony rows across two floor bands

images.title: 105 rue de Rennes, caryatids flanking window
images.author: Fred Romero
images.shows: frontal detail: full-figure sculpted caryatids flanking a piano-nobile window in place of a plain console -- an extreme, dated example of window treatment becoming sculptural rather than just corniced

images.title: 107 rue de Rennes, caryatids flanking window
images.author: Fred Romero
images.shows: frontal detail, the neighbouring building's matching pair of sculpted caryatids at a window -- same treatment as 105 rue de Rennes, confirms it as a deliberate facade-wide scheme rather than a one-off

images.title: 1 bis place de l'Alma, mascaron over porte-cochere
images.author: Neoclassicism Enthusiast
images.shows: sharp frontal close-up of a smiling female mascaron set in a foliate surround above a wrought-iron porte-cochere -- clean example of mascaron-as-standard-ornament over an entrance

images.title: 14 boulevard Saint-Michel, window pediment with mascaron
images.author: Polymagou
images.shows: sharp frontal close-up of a broken-scroll window pediment with a mascaron head at the centre flanked by fruit swags -- textbook combination of the richening pediment and the mascaron becoming standard vocabulary

images.title: Mascaron detail, Paris
images.author: Thomas Bresson (ComputerHotline)
images.shows: very sharp frontal close-up of a bearded male mascaron keystone -- good clean reference for carving style even though the source building/address is not recorded

images.title: 47 rue du Faubourg Montmartre, mascaron keystone over door
images.author: Neoclassicism Enthusiast
images.shows: sharp frontal close-up of a bearded mascaron keystone over a carved segmental-arch door pediment with fruit swags -- another clean pediment+mascaron pairing

images.title: Avenue de l'Opera, no. 38 and neighbours
images.author: Freepenguin
images.shows: whole facade run along a street cut through and built up in the late 1870s-1880s: continuous cornices, alternating triangular/segmental window pediments on the upper floors -- ground floor is cluttered with shopfront signage and a tour bus roofline crosses the bottom

images.title: Rue de la Chaussee-d'Antin, column capitals before/after cleaning
images.author: Tangopaso
images.shows: close frontal detail of two adjacent richly carved Corinthian-order pilaster capitals, one still soot-blackened and one cleaned -- useful for carving depth/style reference; a scaffold pole partly crosses the left capital

images.title: Rue de l'Arbalete, immeuble Villa Medicis
images.author: VVVCFFrance
images.shows: whole facade, shot from below at a moderate upward angle: applied cast floral appliques between windows, a sculpted mascaron and carved console brackets over the porte-cochere, an architect's name plaque (partly legible) set into the facade

notes: Commons metadata almost never records a construction year for these buildings, so `year` is left blank throughout per the no-guessing rule; addresses/arrondissements are recorded where the filename or description gave them. Several strong-looking Commons hits were rejected during review: Avenue Adrien-Hebrard and 35 boulevard Haussmann (Galeries Lafayette) read as later Belle Epoque work, not 1870-1884; 41 rue de Rivoli was too plain/undecorated to evidence this family's richening-ornament claim; two Avenue de l'Opera frames and 51 rue Montorgueil were dropped for a tour-bus obstruction and an interior painted panel respectively; one frame was a night shot. The two rue de Rennes caryatid images are of neighbouring doors on what is very likely the same building elevation -- kept as a pair since it strengthens rather than duplicates the evidence that the sculptural window treatment was a deliberate scheme, not a single showcase feature. Coverage skews toward ornament detail shots (mascarons, pediments, caryatids) over full elevations, which suits the brief (mascarons/pediments) but means roofline (45-degree comble) evidence is thinner -- only images 01, 02, 03 and 21(dropped) showed usable roofline.
